Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re excited about the quality and cost profile; the model looks like a great fit for our recommendation pipeline. Before we greenlight the pilot and ramp traffic, our security and SRE teams require a formal uptime/latency commitment for the critical endpoints used by our real-time recommendations.

Specifically we’re asking for:
- Formalized availability SLA during US business hours (Mon–Fri, 8am–6pm PT): 99.99%
- p95 inference latency <= 90ms for the /v1/infer endpoint for 1–2M qps/month (production traffic profile attached)

Can Redwood confirm feasibility and an estimated timeline to enable this? Attached is a short doc with our traffic pattern and business impact.

Elena

Marcus / team —

Quick technical readout after an initial pass with SRE. Short answer: this is doable, but only under strict operational constraints. Below are the conditions and the tradeoffs we need to surface to the customer.

Required conditions to approach 90ms p95:
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) in the us-west-2 region, pinned to a lower-latency instance class (A100x2 equivalent).
- Model variant: quantized 4-bit optimized variant with fusion kernels; we must pin to this variant for the agreement.
- Request shaping: enforce a max request size and disallow long context (>1024 tokens) for the committed endpoints.
- KV/prefix cache warm-up: 72h of warm traffic or explicit cache preloading during rollout verification.
- Continuous batching disabled for the prioritized pool or capped at very small windows (<=8ms) to avoid batching-induced tail latency.

Operational controls and fallback:
- Primary: prioritized Dedicated pool with 99.99% uptime target during business hours (subject to maintenance windows pre-notified 72h).
- Fallback: automatic routing to a compatible hosted variant (slightly higher p95; typical delta +20–30ms) with traffic-weighted rate limits — this will be our documented fallback and will appear in the SLA as an allowed remediation path.
- Monitoring: per-route p95 telemetry surfaced to both parties; heartbeat alerts and an SLO alert playbook maintained in the MAP.

Constraints and realistic SLO proposal: given the operational constraints above, our recommended contractual commitments are:
- During business hours (Mon–Fri 8am–6pm PT): availability 99.95% and p95 <= 110ms
- Outside business hours: availability 99.9% and p95 <= 150ms

Why we’re not comfortable with 99.99% / 90ms today: that level requires additional guardrails (e.g., dedicated hot-standby capacity and layer of request-side hedging) and will materially increase cost. If Stratus will commit to a 12-month reserved-capacity dollar commitment at a higher tier, we can re-evaluate a 99.99%/90ms promise with a procurement-approved price uplift.

Lead time: 3–4 weeks to provision Dedicated capacity and run a load validation; 1 week to produce MAP + runbook.

I’ve attached a short brief that lists the SLO constraints and the minimal engineering checklist (SLO-constraints-brief.md).

Lauren
